topic: Change of Basis: Viewing the World Through Different Lenses
target_audience: University students or advanced high school students studying Linear Algebra

sections.title: The Concept of 'Perspective'
lecture_lines: One location can be described by different coordinate systems.
The drone follows a grid aligned with the streets.
The bird sees the world through a tilted grid.
Both observers point to the same physical location.
Same spot, but different coordinates based on their perspective.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Standard Basis
lecture_lines: We define grids using standard basis vectors i and j.
Every vector is a combination of these unit vectors.
This standard perspective gives us familiar coordinates like [3, 2].
animations: Fade in a standard grid (#555555) with basis vectors i (#00FF00) and j (#0000FF).
Show vector V = 3i + 2j as a white arrow (#FFFFFF) formed by the sum of 3i and 2j.
Display the coordinate pair [3, 2] in #FFFFFF next to the tip of vector V.

sections.title: Introducing a New Basis
lecture_lines: We can choose an entirely different set of basis vectors.
These new vectors, b1 and b2, form a new basis.
They define a tilted and stretched coordinate grid.
A point at [1, 1] here means one of each.
We reach it by following the new basis vectors.
animations: Show standard grid (#555555) with unit vectors i (#00FF00) and j (#0000FF).
Fade in new basis vectors b1 = [2, 1] (#FF0000) and b2 = [-1, 1] (#FF8C00).
Transform the standard grid into a tilted red grid (#FF0000) aligned with b1 and b2.
Place a white dot (#FFFFFF) at the coordinates [1, 1] in the new basis system.
Draw arrows along b1 then b2 to reach the white dot, showing the linear combination.

sections.title: The Change of Basis Matrix (The Bridge)
lecture_lines: The change of basis matrix acts as a translator.
Its columns are the new basis vectors in standard coordinates.
Each column tells where a new basis unit lands.
animations: Display vectors b1 = [2, 1] and b2 = [-1, 1] with labels in #FFFFFF.

Construct matrix P = [[2, -1], [1, 1]] using b1 and b2 as its columns, incorporating [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg] to represent the transition between basis systems.
Highlight the first column in #FF0000 (b1) and the second in #FF8C00 (b2).

sections.title: The Transformation Formula
lecture_lines: This formula converts new coordinates back to standard ones.
Multiplying by P performs the translation between systems.
The result reveals the point's position in our standard grid.
Matrix P serves as the bridge between these perspectives.
Use P inverse to convert standard coordinates back to new.
animations: Display the formula [v]_std = P * [v]_new in the center of the screen (#FFFFFF).
Animate the multiplication: matrix P [[2, -1], [1, 1]] times vector [1, 1].
Show the result [1, 2] and label it as the 'Standard' coordinates in #FFFFFF.
Highlight the matrix P as the 'Bridge' between the two coordinate systems.
Introduce the inverse formula [v]_new = P^-1 * [v]_std and highlight P^-1 in #FFD700.

sections.title: Visual Summary and Application
lecture_lines: First identify basis, build matrix P, and multiply.
This logic powers rotations and cameras in computer graphics.
Viewing the world through different lenses changes everything.
animations: Display a summary list: 1. Identify Basis, 2. Build Matrix P, 3. Multiply to translate.
